en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tiṇasūlaka Bandhujīvaka Chapter 7 The Apadāna of the Elder Tiṇasūlaka: "I was a woodcutter in the forest, gathering firewood for sale. There, I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, seated at the foot of a tree. With a single blade of grass, I offered him a seat; Because of that deed, I attained the state of an Arhat."
"Not far from the Himālayas is a mountain named Bhūtagaṇa;
The Self-Existent One, who has transcended the world,
I took a blade of grass and offered it to the Buddha.
he was not subject to the lower realms.
I was once a tree upon the earth;
I was a mighty wheel-turning monarch.
[as above] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Tiṇasūlaka spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Tiṇasūlaka.
